Rashi on Gittin 54b:10:1.english: In principle [lit., the line of the law] - That is to say, the law dictates [this]:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:10:2.hebrew: אתה אומר כן - שאינו נאמן? אבל רבי יוחנן אמר משום רבי יוסי כו':
Rashi on Gittin 54b:10:2.english: Do you say this - that he is not deemed credible? Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei, etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:10:3.english: [The Torah] deemed him credible - And even after [some] time [has passed], as [the Gemara] explains:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:11:1.hebrew: כהן גדול ביוה"כ - בפר ושעיר שלפני ולפנים, שהוא שם יחיד ואין רואהו, ואם אמר "פגול" — מהימן; דהא כתיב: "המקריב אותו לא יחשב" (ויקרא ז׳:י״ח), וקרי "לא יחשב" — מחשבת פיגול, ואם חשב — פיגול יהיה:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:11:1.english: The High Priest on Yom Kippur - [This refers to his service] with the bull and the goat of the innermost sanctum, where he is there alone and no one sees him, yet if he says [it is] piggul [disqualifying intent], he is believed. For it is written: "the one who offers it, it shall not be reckoned [to him]" (Leviticus 7:18), and it is read [as "he shall not think"] a thought of piggul, and if he did think [it], it shall be piggul.

Rashi on Gittin 54b:11:2.hebrew: ומנא ידעינן - ביוה"כ דפגיל, אי לאו דמהימן:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:11:2.english: And from where do we know - on Yom Kippur that he rendered [the offering] piggul [disqualified by improper intent], if not that he is believed:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:12:1.hebrew: ודלמא - כי אמר קרא "פיגול יהיה", היינו דשמעינן דפגיל בקול רם, דאמר: "הריני מזה על מנת להקטיר אימורין חוץ לזמנן":
Rashi on Gittin 54b:12:1.english: But perhaps - when the verse says, "It shall be piggul," [it refers to a case] where we heard him render [the offering] piggul in a loud voice, as he said: "Behold, I am sprinkling [the blood] with the intention to burn the sacrificial parts outside their [allotted] time":

Rashi on Gittin 54b:12:2.hebrew: ומשני אי לאו דמהימן - לומר "בשעת עבודה פיגלתי", אע"ג דשמעניה דפגיל, נמי דלמא לבתר עבודה קאמר:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:12:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Were [he] not deemed credible - to say, "During the [Temple] service I rendered [the offering] piggul [disqualified by improper intention]," even though we heard him rendering [it] piggul, still, perhaps he said [it] after the service:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:13:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: דלמא דחזיניה בפישפש - ודלמא בכה"ג מהימן, דחזינן בפישפש דבשעת אמירה היה מזה. פישפש — פתח קטן שהיה בבית החליפות פתוח להיכל, ושנים היו: אחד בצפון ואחד בדרום, כדתניא בזבחים באיזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נה:): שני פישפשין היו בבית החליפות, אחד בצפון ואחד בדרום, כדי להכשיר את כל העזרה לשחיטת קדשים קלים, שנהיה קורין בכל הרוחות "ושחטו פתח אוהל מועד" (ויקרא א׳:ג׳). וגם לול קטן היה פתוח לבית הכפורת. והאי דמקשי הכא "דלמא דחזיניה בפישפש", אהזאות דעל הפרוכת בהיכל קאי; וגבי עבודות דלפני ולפנים נמי איכא לאקשויי דחזיניה דרך לול:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:13:1.english: This is the correct reading: "Perhaps we saw him through a pishpash [small door]" - And perhaps in such a case he is believed, because we saw [him] through the pishpash [and observed] that at the time of [his] statement he was sprinkling [the blood]. A pishpash is a small opening that was in the Chamber of Knives [Beit HaChalifot] open to the Sanctuary [Heichal], and there were two [of them]: one in the north and one in the south, as it is taught in a baraita in Zevachim, [in the chapter] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 55b): "There were two pishpashin in the Chamber of Knives, one in the north and one in the south, in order to render the entire Courtyard fit for the slaughter of offerings of lesser sanctity, so that we may apply [the verse] in all directions, 'And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting' (Leviticus 1:3)." And there was also a small skylight [lul] open to the Holy of Holies [Beit HaKaporet]. And this [question] that [the Gemara] asks here, "Perhaps we saw him through a pishpash," refers to the sprinklings upon the Curtain [Parochet] in the Sanctuary; and regarding the services of the innermost sanctum [the Holy of Holies] as well, one could ask that we saw him through the skylight:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:14:1.english: And you are not deemed credible, etc. - since [it] is not in your possession:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:16:1.hebrew: ולעבר עלייהו קולמוס - לשמן, כתב על גבי כתב, ולקדשיה:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:16:1.english: And let him pass a reed pen over them - With proper intention for them, [as] writing over writing, and sanctify them:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:17:1.hebrew: ולא הטיל בו דלת - ונמצא שם כתוב כדרכו, אבל שלא לשמו הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:17:1.english: And did not place a dalet in it - and [thus the Divine] Name is found written in its normal manner, but it is not [written] for its sake:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:17:2.english: He passes a reed pen over it - for its sake [i.e., for the sake of God's Name]:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:18:1.hebrew: כוליה ס"ת - כל אזכרות שבו:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:18:1.english: An entire Torah scroll - [meaning] all the mentions [of God's name] in it:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:1:1.hebrew: נפלו ונתפצעו - אגוזי פרך אין בטלין אפילו באלף, מפני חשיבותן. נתפצעו האגוזים של ערלה ואח"כ נפלו לתוך של היתר — יעלו; וכאן נפלו תחלה ואח"כ נתפצעו:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:1:1.english: They fell and were cracked - Perekh nuts are not nullified even in a thousand [parts] because of their significance. If the orlah nuts were cracked and afterward fell into permitted [nuts], they are nullified; [whereas here,] they fell first and afterward were cracked:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:1:2.hebrew: אחד - שפצען שוגג, שלא נתכוין כדי לבטל חשיבותן ולהעלותן באחד ומאתים כדין ערלה, בין שפצען מזיד, שנתכוין לכך:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:1:2.english: Whether - he cracked them unintentionally, [meaning] that he did not intend to nullify their significance and [thereby] cause them to be nullified in [a ratio of] one [to] two hundred as is the law of orlah, or whether he cracked them intentionally, [meaning] that he intended to do so:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:1:3.hebrew: לא יעלו - אפילו באלף, דקניס ר"מ ורבי יהודה שוגג אטו מזיד, אע"ג דהך עלייה, שהוא מעלה ומבטל אגוזי פרך, איסורא דרבנן בעלמא הוא, ואפילו שלמים; דמדאורייתא אין חילוק בין חשוב לשאינו חשוב, דהכל בטל, דכתיב (שמות כ״ג:ב׳): "אחרי רבים להטות", ורבנן הוא דגזור:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:1:3.english: They are not nullified - even in a thousand [parts], for Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah penalize an unintentional [act] on account of an intentional [act], even though this [prohibition against] nullification—[that] one nullifies and neutralizes nuts of Perekh—is merely a rabbinic prohibition, even [when they are] whole; for by Torah law there is no distinction between something significant and something not significant, as everything is nullified [in a majority], as it is written (Exodus 23:2): "After a majority to incline," and it is the Rabbis who decreed [it]:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:2:1.hebrew: דאתי לאיערומי - ולהתכוין, ויאמר: "שוגג הייתי ולא נתכוונתי כדי להעלותן":
Rashi on Gittin 54b:2:1.english: That he will come to employ artifice - and [act] intentionally, and he will say: "I acted unintentionally and did not intend [to do so] in order to nullify them":

Rashi on Gittin 54b:3:1.hebrew: הרי זה לא ילקט - דכל זמן שהיא במקומה, כמחובר חשיבא ולא בטלה, וכי לקיט לפירות ומבטל להו במאתים, הוי מבטל איסור לכתחילה:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:3:1.english: He may not gather - For as long as it [the sapling] is in its place, it is considered as attached [to the ground] and is not nullified, and when he gathers the fruits and nullifies them in two hundred, he is nullifying a prohibition from the outset:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:3:2.english: And if he gathered - and did not consult [a sage]:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:3:3.hebrew: יעלו - דה"ל שוגג, דלא נתכוון ללקט ע"מ לבטל, דסבור שכבר בטלו במחובר:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:3:3.english: They are nullified - for he is [considered] an unwitting [transgressor], since he did not intend to gather [them] in order to nullify [the forbidden produce], as he thought that they were already nullified while [still] attached [to the ground]:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:3:4.english: Provided that he does not intend to gather - with the intention of nullification:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:4:1.english: Even one who intends [to gather], etc. - Thus, [even] intentionally it is also nullified:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:5:1.hebrew: אין אדם אוסר את כרמו בנטיעה אחת - אין לך אדם נוטע ערלה בין שאר נטיעות בלא סימן ואוסר כרמו בשביל נטיעה אחת, וכיון דלא שכיחא, לא אחמור בה רבנן; אבל נפילת איסור בהיתר, שכיחא:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:5:1.english: A person does not render his vineyard forbidden for the sake of one sapling - There is no person who plants orlah among other saplings without a marker and renders his vineyard forbidden for the sake of one sapling, and since it is uncommon, the Rabbis were not stringent regarding it; whereas [the] falling of forbidden [produce] into permitted [produce] is common:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:8:1.english: Whatever is in his power - to do at the time that he informs him:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:8:2.hebrew: נאמן - ורישא, כגון שעודן בידו לטמאן ולפגלן. וגבי קרבנות, בכהן העובד קמיירי — כגון שהודיעו בין שחיטה לזריקה, ואמר: "פיגלתיה בשחיטה", שעדיין בידו לפגלו בשאר עבודות. אבל ביום פלוני, שכבר יצאו מידו, לאו כל כמיניה:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:8:2.english: [He is] deemed credible - And the first clause [refers to a case] where they are still in his power to render them ritually impure or to render them piggul [disqualified by improper intention]. And regarding sacrifices, [the baraita] is speaking of the officiating priest — for example, where he informed him between the slaughter and the sprinkling [of the blood], and said, "I rendered it piggul during the slaughter," for it is still in his power to render it piggul during the remaining [sacrificial] services. However, [when he speaks of] "such-and-such a day," when they have already left his power, it is not within his authority [to be believed]:

Rashi on Gittin 54b:9:1.hebrew: רבא אמר - אע"פ שאין בידו, נאמן; וסיפא, כגון דאשכחיה מקמי האידנא ולא אמר ליה, והשתא א"ל:
Rashi on Gittin 54b:9:1.english: Rava said - Even though [it is] not in his power, he is believed; and the latter clause [deals with a case] where he found him earlier and did not tell him, and now he tells him:

Tosafot on Gittin 54b:11:1.hebrew: דכי אמר פיגול מהימן - ותימה: הא רבי יוסי גופיה בזבחים פרק בית שמאי (זבחים דף מד:) אית ליה דאין פיגול בדבר הנעשה בפנים, דיליף משלמים! וי"ל: נהי דפיגול לא הוי, פסול מיהא הוי, ו"פיגול" דהכא לאו דוקא, כדאשכחן בסוף פ"ק דזבחים (דף יד.) לרבי [שמעון] דאמר: כל שאינו על מזבח החיצון כשלמים אין חייבין עליו משום פיגול, ואמר רבי יוסי בר' חנינא: מודה רבי [שמעון] דפסול מקל וחומר. ואין לתמוה מנא ליה דמהימן, דפשיטא דבכל הקרבנות שייך פיגול בכל ד' עבודות:
Tosafot on Gittin 54b:11:1.english: As when he says [it is] piggul, he is believed - And this is puzzling: Rabbi Yose himself holds in Zevachim, chapter Beit Shammai (Zevachim 44b), that there is no piggul in something performed inside [the Sanctuary], as he derives [this] from peace-offerings! And one can answer: granted that it is not piggul, it is nevertheless disqualified, and "piggul" here is not exact — just as we find at the end of the first chapter of Zevachim (14a), according to Rabbi [Shimon], who says: Anything that is not [offered] on the outer altar like peace-offerings, one is not liable for it on account of piggul; and Rabbi Yose bar Rabbi Ḥanina said: Rabbi [Shimon] concedes that it is disqualified through an a fortiori argument. And one should not wonder from where he knows that he is believed, for it is obvious that in all offerings piggul applies to all four services:

Tosafot on Gittin 54b:1:1.hebrew: נפלו ונתפצעו - תימה, דתניא בירושלמי בפרק בתרא דערלה: נפלו ואח"כ נתפצעו, בין בשוגג בין במזיד לא יעלו, דברי ר"מ; ורבי יהודה אומר: בין בשוגג בין במזיד יעלו; ורבי יוסי אומר: שוגג יעלו, מזיד לא יעלו. טעמא דר"מ דקניס שוגג אטו מזיד; טעמא דרבי יוסי כדאמר רבי אבהו בשם ר' יוחנן: כל האיסורין שריבה עליהם, שוגג מותר, מזיד אסור; טעמא דרבי יהודה מפרש: משום דכבר קנסו בידו — פירוש, כבר נתקלקלו פירותיו בשעת פציעה:
Tosafot on Gittin 54b:1:1.english: They fell and were broken - This is astonishing, for it is taught in the Jerusalem Talmud in the last chapter of Orlah: If they fell and afterward were broken, whether unintentionally or intentionally, they are not nullified — [these are] the words of Rabbi Meir; and Rabbi Yehuda says: Whether unintentionally or intentionally, they are nullified; and Rabbi Yosei says: Unintentionally, they are nullified; intentionally, they are not nullified. Rabbi Meir's reason is that he penalizes an unintentional [act] on account of an intentional [act]. Rabbi Yosei's reason is in accordance with what Rabbi Abahu said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: Regarding all forbidden items upon which one increased [the permitted mixture to nullify them], [if done] unintentionally it is permitted, [if done] intentionally it is forbidden. Rabbi Yehuda's reason, [the Jerusalem Talmud] explains, is because his penalty is already in his hand — meaning, his produce was already ruined at the time of breaking:

Tosafot on Gittin 54b:8:1.hebrew: אמר אביי כל שבידו נאמן - הקשה ר"ת: דהכא אפי' לרבא לא מהימן אלא משום שהיה בידו תחילה, ובפ' האומר (קידושין דף סו.) פליגי אביי ורבא באשתו זינתה בעד אחד והלה שותק, ומשמע התם דתרוייהו מודו בא"ל עד אחד "נטמאו טהרותיך" והלה שותק — נאמן, וכן א"ל עד אחד "אכלת חלב", ואע"ג דאין בידו! ואומר ר"ת דהכא במכחישו, או אומר איני יודע, אבל התם דשותק הוי כהודאה; וכן משמע בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף פז:) דבעי למיפשט מיניה דעד אחד נאמן באיסורין, ודחי: דלמא שאני הכא משום דאשתיק, ושתיקה כהודאה דמיא. וגבי אשתו זינתה פליגי נמי בשותק, ומהני לאביי בעד אחד כשר דלאו גזלנא, אף ע"ג דאין דבר שבערוה פחות משנים, או בקינוי וסתירה בעד אחד — הכא דשותק שאני, אי נמי מדרבנן; ורבא אפי' שותק לא אסר, אלא אם כן מהימן עליה כבי תרי. ומתוך כך אומר ר"ת דאדם המטהר יין לחברו, אי אשכחיה ואמר ליה בזימנא קמייתא, מהימן כרבא ואפילו מכחישו, כיון דהיה בידו; אבל אחר לא מהימן אי מכחישו או אומר איני יודע, ואי שתיק מהימן — וכן פסק רבינו משולם בן רבינו קלונימוס — ואי מהימן עליה כבי תרי אסור, כדאשכחן בהוא סמיא (קדושין דף סו.) לרבא; ואפי' היכא דלא מהימן, מכל מקום לדידיה אסור, דשויא אנפשיה חתיכה דאיסורא. ונראה דאם שותק מחמת שאינו יודע, דלא הויא שתיקה כהודאה, וכל הסוגיא דקידושין יש לפרש באומר לו "נטמאו טהרותיך בפניך" או "ידעת", תדע דקתני דומיא ד"אכלת חלב", והתם דוקא הויא שתיקה כהודאה:
Tosafot on Gittin 54b:8:1.english: Abaye said: Whenever it is in his power, he is deemed credible - Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: Here, even according to Rava, he is not deemed credible except because it was in his power initially; yet in the chapter [entitled] HaOmer (Kiddushin 66a), Abaye and Rava disagree regarding [a case where one witness testified] "Your wife committed adultery" with one witness and the other [the husband] is silent, and it is implied there that both of them agree regarding [a case where] one witness said to him, "Your ritually pure foods became impure," and the other is silent — [the witness] is deemed credible; and similarly [where] one witness said to him, "You ate forbidden fat," even though it is not in his power! And Rabbeinu Tam says that here [in our Gemara] it is speaking of [a case where] he contradicts him or says "I do not know," whereas there, where he is silent, it is like an admission. And so too it is implied in HaIsha Rabba (Yevamot 87b), where [the Gemara] seeks to resolve from it that one witness is deemed credible in [matters of] ritual prohibitions, and rejects [this]: Perhaps here it is different because he was silent, and silence is like an admission. And regarding "His wife committed adultery," they likewise disagree where he is silent: and according to Abaye it is effective with one valid witness who is not a robber — even though there is no matter of forbidden sexual relations [established] with fewer than two [witnesses], or [only] with warning (kinui) and seclusion (setirah) with one witness — here, where he is silent, it is different, or alternatively [it is effective] by rabbinic law; whereas Rava does not prohibit [her] even when he is silent, unless he relies upon him like two [witnesses]. And from this Rabbeinu Tam says that [regarding] a person who prepares wine in ritual purity for his fellow: if he found him and told him at the first occasion, he is deemed credible according to Rava even if he contradicts him, since it was in his power; however, afterward he is not deemed credible if he contradicts him or says "I do not know," though if he is silent he is deemed credible — and so ruled Rabbeinu Meshullam ben Rabbeinu Kalonymus — and if he relies upon him like two [witnesses], it is prohibited, as we find with that blind man (Kiddushin 66a) according to Rava. And even where he is not deemed credible, nevertheless for himself [the witness] it is prohibited, because he has rendered it a piece of forbidden [food] for himself. And it seems that if he is silent because he does not know, silence is not like an admission; and the entire sugya of Kiddushin can be explained as speaking of [a case where] he says to him, "Your ritually pure foods became impure in your presence" or "You know [it]" — know [that this is so], for it teaches [this] in a manner similar to "You ate forbidden fat," and there specifically silence is like an admission:
